purpose: Shopify feed operational realism replay pack extended with harder real-failure cases from the same incident family.

cases.title: Variant shape looked plausible until size silently disappeared from the export
cases.symptom: A product family with multiple colors and sizes failed Shopify sync with missing-option and duplicate-variant style errors even though the transformed export still looked superficially complete.
visible_evidence: Raw source rows clearly carry both color and size information
The transformed export path preserves one variant dimension but silently loses another
The push error surface points at variant shape correctness, not one obviously bad row
A local dedupe tweak would be tempting but would not explain why declared product options and variant values drift apart

entry_points: transform field mapping for variant dimensions
starting_context.repro_style: multi-color multi-size apparel export where one hidden dimension disappears before sync

misleading_telemetry: the exported rows still look populated enough to seem valid at first glance
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: patch duplicate handling only and assume the source data itself is fine

success_criteria: identify that variant option loss happened before the final Shopify push rather than only at the point of duplicate rejection
propose a fix family that preserves the missing dimension and keeps declared option names and values aligned through export
cases.notes: Concrete inspiration: Luna pant and similar multi-size apparel failures from the 2026-05-01 J.Crew push report.

cases.title: A single product seemed to have four option names when it really had one drifting label
cases.symptom: Shopify rejected a product for exceeding the option limit because row-level option names drifted by color or pattern even though the underlying dimension was still just color plus size.
visible_evidence: One handle shows Option1 Name values like Black, Blue, Brown, and Woven Pattern 5 across rows
The actual row structure still reads like one color dimension plus one size dimension
The visible failure can tempt a broad exporter rewrite because the platform reports an options-count problem

starting_context.repro_style: single-handle option-name drift causing apparent too-many-options failure

misleading_telemetry: the product has only two human-meaningful dimensions
the platform error mentions maximum options instead of label drift
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: broaden into a full product-options redesign instead of normalizing one unstable name field

success_criteria: identify that the problem is unstable option naming rather than true four-dimension product structure
match the compact normalization fix family around stable names like Color and Size
cases.notes: Concrete inspiration: Cosmo pant and Garcon shirt option-limit failures.

cases.title: Duplicate variant errors looked like duplicate rows but were really collapsed tuples
cases.symptom: Shopify reported that variants like WHITE or BLACK already existed, even though the source rows differed by size and did not appear truly duplicated in the raw feed.
visible_evidence: Several failing handles have one color repeated across many rows with different sizes
The duplicate string in the error matches color, not the full intended variant tuple
The quickest wrong move is to delete rows or dedupe on color only

starting_context.repro_style: single-color multi-size products collapse into duplicate variant keys

misleading_telemetry: the duplicate error names only the visible color value
the raw feed does not obviously contain exact duplicate rows
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: dedupe harder on the visible duplicate value without restoring the full variant tuple

success_criteria: identify that the duplicate key is being computed from an incomplete tuple
match the narrow fix family of deduping on full option tuples after preserving all option values
cases.notes: Concrete inspiration: boyfriend jersey tees and similar duplicate-color failures.

cases.title: Accessory variants failed on a string that looked descriptive but violated platform rules
cases.symptom: Several accessory products failed despite otherwise simple one-size structure because an option name containing a slash sequence was passed through unsanitized.
visible_evidence: Affected handles are simple accessories rather than deep multi-variant apparel products
The same visible string ACCESSORIES / MULTI appears in the option-name position
The failure is deterministic and repeats across multiple handles with otherwise uncomplicated structure

starting_context.repro_style: simple accessory export rejected for unsupported sequence in option name

success_criteria: identify that the failure sits in option-name sanitization rather than in batching or broad variant logic
match the localized fix family that remaps or sanitizes unsupported sequences before export
cases.notes: Concrete inspiration: ACCESSORIES / MULTI failures on bag and sunglasses handles.

cases.title: Throttling dominated the receipt and hid a second class of deterministic shape failures
cases.symptom: A large push returned many throttled product failures plus a smaller set of deterministic data-shape errors, making it unsafe to treat retry success as proof that the feed was healthy.
visible_evidence: Most failed products are marked Throttled
A non-trivial minority fail with duplicate, missing-option, or invalid-name errors in the same consolidated receipt
Chunk transport itself succeeds, so the transport layer is not globally broken
A pure backoff fix would improve many outcomes while still leaving a hidden validation class unresolved

entry_points: result classifier for throttled vs deterministic errors
starting_context.repro_style: batch push where transport pressure and deterministic validation failures coexist

misleading_telemetry: throttling dominates the top-line error count
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: slow the push and claim the incident is resolved once throttling drops

success_criteria: separate retryable execution pressure from deterministic feed-shape failures
propose a fix family that improves batching while preserving fast failure and reporting for validation bugs
cases.notes: Concrete inspiration: 133 throttled failures mixed with 60 non-throttle data failures in the same push receipt.

cases.title: A first fix looked right because the transport succeeded, but the variant evidence kept disagreeing
cases.symptom: A repair pass made the push path look healthier, yet later inspection still showed the variant tuple was wrong and the apparent success was misleading.
visible_evidence: The push request returns normally after a repair attempt
Variant evidence is still inconsistent across the transformed export and the final receipt
The easiest wrong move is to treat the recovered transport as proof the data shape is now correct

starting_context.repro_style: first repair appears successful but later evidence contradicts it

misleading_telemetry: repair path emits optimistic progress markers
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: accept the first repaired receipt as evidence the shape problem is gone

success_criteria: identify why the first success signal was not enough to clear the variant-shape bug
keep the fix grounded in the data-shape path, not transport optimism
cases.notes: New adversarial case from the same incident family, focused on false confidence after a repair pass.

cases.title: Logs pointed at the wrong layer while the real break happened during option assembly
cases.symptom: The visible failure looked like a downstream push issue, but the actual bug surfaced earlier when option assembly mixed stable and unstable labels.
visible_evidence: The failure surface is downstream and noisy
The option builder already emitted inconsistent labels before the push
A local retry or push-only patch would miss the earlier misassembly

starting_context.repro_style: wrong-layer logging that makes the push surface look guilty

misleading_telemetry: option names already drift before the push layer sees them
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: patch only the downstream push code because that is where the loudest error appears

success_criteria: identify the earlier option-assembly bug behind the downstream symptom
match a fix family that addresses the true source of label drift
cases.notes: New case focused on wrong-layer attribution.

cases.title: A partial mitigation improved the batch but left one hidden size path broken
cases.symptom: A mitigation reduced visible failures, but one variant path still broke later because the hidden size dimension was never restored end-to-end.
visible_evidence: The batch appears healthier after a local mitigation
One hidden dimension still goes missing on a narrower subset of rows
The easy mistake is to declare victory after the broader error count drops

starting_context.repro_style: partial fix reduces noise while a subset stays broken

misleading_telemetry: one variant path still disagrees with the expected tuple
replay_augmentation.false_positive_fix_family: stop once the count drops instead of checking the remaining hidden-size path

success_criteria: identify the remaining hidden-size path that stayed broken
keep the fix anchored to end-to-end tuple preservation
cases.notes: New case for false confidence after a partial mitigation.
